## Citation reach

*Updated: `r reach_month(reach$as_of)`*

Where, and in which disciplines, my work is cited. The figures come from
[OpenAlex](https://openalex.org/authors/A5015716464), an open index of
scholarly works, and cover the works it records as citing my publications.

<details class="method">
<summary>About these figures</summary>

- OpenAlex links `r t$my_works` works to my ORCID iD. A citation is a work that
  cites one of them; a work citing two of them counts twice, as in OpenAlex's own
  totals. `r t$self_citing_works` of the `r reach_num(t$citing_works)` citing works are my own.
- Disciplines and subdisciplines are the fields and subfields of each citing
  work's main topic in OpenAlex's classification (domains, fields, subfields and
  topics). `r reach_num(t$citations_without_topic)` citations come from works OpenAlex has
  not classified: they are left out of the discipline charts and shown as
  Unclassified in the chart by year.
- Citing scholars are the authors of the citing works, other than me, each counted
  once in each country of the institutions they list. `r reach_num(t$works_without_country)`
  of the citing works list no institution, so their authors have no country.
  Countries too small to see on the map are shown as dots.
- The years run from `r t$first_year`, when my first work appeared; the
  `r t$citations_before_first_year` citations OpenAlex dates earlier are dating
  errors and are left out. The latest year is counted to `r reach_month(reach$as_of)`.
- The figures are refreshed from OpenAlex whenever the site is rebuilt.

</details>

```{r}
#| output: asis
reach_html(reach_kpis())
```

## Countries

Where the scholars citing my work are based, by the institutions they list on
the citing works. Hover over a country to see its numbers.

```{r}
#| output: asis
reach_html(reach_map())
```

The `r reach$top_countries` countries with the most citing scholars:

```{r}
#| output: asis
reach_html(reach_bars(top_countries, "name", "scholars"))
reach_html(reach_table(sprintf("All %d countries", t$countries), c("Country", "Citing scholars", "Citing works"),
                       lapply(reach$countries, function(c) list(c$name, c$scholars, c$works))))
```

## Disciplines

Citations by the discipline of the citing work: the field of its main topic in
OpenAlex's classification of research.

```{r}
#| output: asis
reach_html(reach_bars(reach$fields, "name", "citations"))
reach_html(reach_table("As a table", c("Discipline", "Citations", "Share"),
                       lapply(reach$fields, function(f) list(f$name, f$citations, paste0(f$share, "%")))))
```

## Subdisciplines

The `r reach$top_subfields` subdisciplines (OpenAlex's subfields) with the most
citations. The colours are those of the chart by year below, where the smaller
subdisciplines are grouped as Other.

```{r}
#| output: asis
reach_html(reach_bars(top_subfields, "name", "citations"))
reach_html(reach_table(sprintf("All %d subdisciplines", length(reach$subfields)),
                       c("Subdiscipline", "Discipline", "Citations"),
                       lapply(reach$subfields, function(s) list(s$name, s$field, s$citations))))
```

## Citations by year

Citations each year, by the year the citing work was published, divided by
subdiscipline. Hover over a bar to see its numbers.

```{r}
#| output: asis
reach_html(paste(reach_years(), collapse = ""))
reach_html(reach_year_table())
```
